audit.reasoning: Coding 'fixed-strict, initial, word domain' rests on the standard reference grammar (Rennison 1997, Routledge Descriptive Grammars, 541 pp.), whose Stress section states twice that word stress is always/constantly on the first syllable, with no lexical tone and no mobile word stress; loans from Moore follow the native pattern. All quoted sentences were verified verbatim at the stated printed pages (430-431) in the held extraction. Glottolog and Crossref show no newer grammar, phonology monograph, JIPA illustration or instrumental study of Koromfe prosody; the only other phonology item (Rennison 1999 syllable chapter) is by the same author and paywalled. One caveat worth keeping in a caution field rather than a reclassify: Rennison himself says word stress is phonetically 'quite weak' and phrase-level prominence is a high pitch on the final full-vowel syllable of the first stressable word, so
